cities.base: Any mid-range hotel near the airport road, this is a one-night crash landing not a stay
cities.name: Amman

cities.base: Wadi Musa, walkable to the Petra entrance gate
cities.name: Petra (Wadi Musa)

cities.base: Bedouin desert camp inside the protected area, booked as part of the jeep tour package
cities.name: Wadi Rum

cities.base: A resort on the eastern shore, close to Amman Beach and about an hour from the airport
cities.name: Dead Sea

places.name: Khazali Canyon
places.note: Narrow cleft you walk into on foot, Thamudic and Nabataean inscriptions scratched into the rock walls. Included on almost every jeep tour, bring a flashlight for the darker sections.

places.name: Red Sand Dune
places.note: Big run of soft red dune against a rock face, everyone stops to climb it and slide back down. Sand gets in everything, worth it once.

places.name: Burdah Rock Bridge hike
places.note: Steep scramble to one of the desert's natural rock arches, 3 to 4 hours round trip with real exposure near the top. Needs a guide and a separate booking, not on the standard jeep circuit; map point is rounded, so let the driver navigate.

places.name: Zarb dinner and stargazing, Desert Bird Camp
places.note: Three-hour evening tour: 4x4 from Wadi Rum Village, meat and vegetables dug up from the sand oven, then stargazing, no overnight. $34 a head on Expedia; start time not published, so confirm it when booking.
places.neighborhood: Desert Bird Camp, 4x4 from Wadi Rum Village

places.name: Stargazing at Desert Bird Camp
places.note: The stargazing half of the $34 Desert Bird Camp dinner tour, so no extra charge if you book that. Walk a few minutes away from the camp lights; worth staying up past dinner for even when tired.

places.name: Um Fruth Rock Bridge
places.note: Smaller and easier rock bridge than Burdah, quick climb with a short exposed step at the top. Common jeep tour add-on, fine for most fitness levels.

places.name: Amman Beach Tourism Resort
places.note: Public beach, cheaper than resort day passes, gets crowded on Fridays with local families. Showers and mud on site are basic, bring your own towel.

places.name: Dead Sea Panorama Complex
places.note: Home of the Dead Sea Museum, on the geology and history of the sea, with a terrace over the whole basin. Entry 1 to 2 JOD at the door per reviewers; hours not confirmed, so check. Good too-hot-to-float filler.

places.name: Mount Nebo
places.note: Where Moses is said to have seen the Promised Land. The Memorial Church, begun in the late 4th century and rebuilt in 597, keeps peacock and zebu floor mosaics; Fantoni's serpent cross stands outside. Jericho usually shows. 3 JOD, do not count on the Jordan Pass; 08:00 to 17:00.

places.name: Oleastro Olive Oil Museum
places.note: Small private museum on olive oil production in the Jordan Valley with a shop and tasting. Off the direct route from Wadi Rum, only worth it if you're coming via the north.

places.name: Bethany Beyond the Jordan (Al-Maghtas)
places.note: UNESCO site since 2015 at the traditional baptism site of Jesus: Elijah's Hill with a 5th-century monastery, the John the Baptist church, pools and steps from about 570. Shuttle and guided walk to the river. 12 JOD and 08:00 to 16:00 from an undated page, so check.

places.name: Dead Sea shoreline at sunset
places.note: The hills of the West Bank and Jerusalem's lights turn pink and gold across the water. Any resort's public shore stretch works, no ticket needed if you're not entering a beach club, just walk the access road at golden hour.

places.name: Ma'in Hot Springs (Hammamat Ma'in)
places.note: Waterfall fed by hot mineral springs, about 30-40 minutes up into the hills from the Dead Sea shore. Public pools can be crowded and a little worn, but the waterfall itself is legitimate and warm, not staged. Good alternate half-day if you're not doing Mujib.

places.name: Dead Sea cosmetics shops (Sweimeh strip)
places.note: Roadside shops selling mud and mineral products, mostly the same stock as the resort gift shops at lower prices. Fine for last-minute souvenirs, nothing you can't get at the airport duty free at similar markup.

places.name: Resort private beach day pass (Kempinski / Marriott / Hilton)
places.note: Cleaner sand and fresher water access than the public beach, with pools, loungers and showers included. Non-guest day passes run $50-80 depending on the property and season, worth it if you're not sleeping at one already.

places.name: Amman Beach float
places.note: Do not shave or shower with any cut first, it stings in a way nobody adequately warns you about.

places.name: Amman Citadel
places.note: The hill holds the Temple of Hercules (AD 161 to 166), the Umayyad Palace (about 735) and the Archaeological Museum, all on one 3 JOD ticket, free with the Jordan Pass, plus the best view over downtown. 08:00 to 17:00 in winter; late afternoon light is best.

places.name: Roman Theater
places.note: 2nd-century theater of about 6,000 seats with a Greek inscription to Antoninus Pius. Stand in the middle of the orchestra and speak: the echo carries, step off and it vanishes. The stage takes the sun, the seats sit in shade. 08:00 to 17:00; folk museums in both wings.

places.name: Rainbow Street
places.note: Cafes, small shops, and a genuine evening buzz after dark. Good option for a jet-lagged first night when you don't want to think, just walk and eat.

places.name: Hashem Restaurant
places.note: No-menu falafel and hummus joint open nearly around the clock, plastic chairs on the street. Cheap, fast, and reliably good, a sensible first meal off a long flight.

places.name: Sufra Restaurant
places.note: Set in a restored villa on Rainbow Street, does mansaf and mezze well in a nicer setting than most tourist-facing Jordanian food. A step up if you want one sit-down dinner in Amman rather than street food.

places.name: The Jordan Museum
places.note: Holds Dead Sea Scrolls fragments and the Ain Ghazal statues, among the oldest human statues found anywhere. Open 09:00 to 17:00, Fridays 15:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesdays; 5 JOD for foreign visitors, not covered by the Jordan Pass.

places.name: Souk Jara
places.note: Friday-only summer street market on Rainbow Street selling crafts and food. Only useful if your one Amman evening happens to fall on a Friday, which for an arrival-night itinerary it usually won't.

places.name: King Abdullah I Mosque
places.note: Blue mosaic dome seen across the city, open to non-Muslim visitors outside prayer times. 2 JOD, not on the Jordan Pass. Women cover head, arms and legs (a gown is lent free), men wear long trousers. Hours follow prayer times, so check; a 30 minute stop.

places.name: Wild Jordan Center Cafe
places.note: Terrace cafe run by the Royal Society for Conservation of Nature, looks down over downtown Amman's rooftops. Quiet spot for a coffee if you need to sit somewhere that isn't a restaurant.

places.name: Abu Darwish Mosque
places.note: Striking black-and-white striped mosque on Amman's highest hill, but it's a detour with little else nearby and the interior isn't generally open to non-worshippers. Photo from outside is the whole visit.

places.name: Downtown Amman viewpoint (Jabal al-Qal'a stairs)
places.note: Free lookout below the Citadel over the amphitheater and downtown rooftops, best right before sunset when the call to prayer starts echoing across the hills.

places.name: Royal Automobile Museum
places.note: Late King Hussein's car collection, well presented but out of the way and low priority on a one-evening Amman stop. Only worth it if you're a car person with time to spare.

places.name: The Siq & Treasury (Al-Khazneh)
places.note: The 1.2km Siq walk into the Treasury is why people come. Arrive at opening, before 10am it turns into a wall of tour groups. Winter hours 06:30 to 17:00 (2 Oct to 1 Mar); summer 06:00 to 18:00.

places.name: Petra by Night
places.note: Candlelit walk through the Siq to the Treasury, mats, mint tea and a bit of music. Sunday to Thursday, 20:30 to 22:30, 30 JOD, children under 10 free. Slower and dimmer than the photos but you would regret skipping it.

places.name: Royal Tombs (Urn, Silk, Corinthian, Palace)
places.note: Facades cut into the cliff on the east side of the basin, with less crush than the Treasury. Covered by the Petra ticket counted on the Siq row, so check the price there. Best late afternoon when the stone goes orange-pink; site closes 17:00 in winter.

places.name: Street of Facades & Theater
places.note: Theater carved into the rock plus a row of tomb facades on the walk into the basin; fold it into the main walk. Covered by the Petra ticket counted on the Siq row, so check the price there. Site closes 17:00 in winter.

places.name: Petra Museum
places.note: Free entry, near the visitor centre at the Petra gate. Good for a midday heat break or rain, it explains the carvings you walked past. Listed 08:30 to 19:30; not confirmed whether a Petra ticket is needed to reach it.

places.name: Little Petra (Siq al-Barid)
places.note: A small version of the Siq about 15 minutes by taxi from Wadi Musa, free entry. Winter hours 07:00 to 14:00 (summer to 16:00), so go in the morning; skippable if time is tight, it repeats what the main site shows.

places.name: Al-Khubtha Trail viewpoint over the Treasury
places.note: Climb up behind the Treasury for the view looking down on its roof, the classic postcard angle. Steep and narrow in places, not for anyone uneasy with exposure.

places.name: The Petra Kitchen
places.note: Hands-on Jordanian cooking session and dinner, books up in advance. A better evening than another hotel buffet if you're staying two nights in Wadi Musa.

places.name: Al-Qantarah Restaurant
places.note: Straightforward Jordanian grill and mezze in town, a reliable dinner after a long day in the park without the tour-bus setting.

places.name: Camel/donkey rides inside Petra
places.note: Skip. Animals are visibly overworked and underfed, the routes are short enough to walk, and the hard sell for tips at the end sours what should be a good moment. Walk it instead.

places.name: Wadi Rum Jeep Tour (Zalabia Bedouin operators)
places.note: About 4.5 hours from the Visitor Centre: Seven Pillars, Red Sand Dune, Um Fruth, Lawrence's House and a meal, $57 a head on Expedia. A private jeep runs 55 to 65 JOD per vehicle for half a day; every driver hits the same stops.
places.neighborhood: Starts at the Wadi Rum Visitor Centre

places.name: Wadi Rum Visitor Centre
places.note: Where you pay the 5 JOD protected area fee and meet or hire a driver, with a view of the Seven Pillars of Wisdom. Winter 08:00 to 16:00, summer to 18:00; arrive early if the jeep tour starts here.

places.name: Lawrence's Spring (Ain Shallaleh)
places.note: Small spring T.E. Lawrence supposedly wrote about, open around the clock, with a short scramble up for a view over the wadi. The spring itself is unremarkable, the view is the point.

places.name: Shawerma Reem
places.note: The Amman shawarma counter, 4.1 on Google from 9,000 reviews: a regular sandwich is 1.25 JOD, a large 1.75. Open until 03:30, from 11:00 on Fridays, so it works for a late arrival.

places.name: Petra Cabin Restaurant
places.note: Jordanian buffet near the Petra gate, 4.7 on Google: dinner buffet 7 JOD, breakfast 5. Listed hours are muddled (Monday shows 09:00 to 12:30) and winter opening is not confirmed, so check before walking over.

places.name: FoodEx Wadi Rum
places.note: Buffet restaurant next to the Visitor Centre, 4.7 on Google: 12 JOD a head. The one sit-down lunch before or after the jeep tour; closes at 19:00, so dinner is at camp.
places.neighborhood: Wadi Rum Village, by the Visitor Centre

places.name: Al Shami Restaurant, Aqaba
places.note: Levantine place in Aqaba, not Rum: about an hour's drive each way, so only for a coast day or the drive out. 4.4 on Google from 2,573 reviews; about 5 JOD a head from a Feb 2026 review (15 JOD for three), no menu price seen.

places.name: Wadi Rum Protected Area
places.note: The UNESCO desert itself, 4.7 on Google from 12,754 reviews. The 5 JOD entry is paid once at the Visitor Centre and counted on that row; check the price there. Late afternoon light is the reason to be out.

places.name: Bacchus, Hilton Dead Sea
places.note: Italian trattoria inside the Hilton: pasta 10 to 16 JOD, mains 20 to 33, plus 14% tax and service. Order the slow-baked lamb shank or the carbonara, about 14 JOD all in.

places.name: Spectrum, Hilton Dead Sea
places.note: Breakfast only as far as the hotel shows: a la carte to 10:30, buffet to 11:00. Eggs benedict 6 JOD, steak and eggs 9, plus 14%. Point is from a third-party listing.

places.name: The Obelisk, Kempinski Ishtar
places.note: The Kempinski buffet: dinner 18:30 to 22:00 at 29 JOD plus tax and service, lunch 13:00 to 16:00 at 27 JOD. Map point is the hotel, not the restaurant.

places.name: Temple of Hercules (Great Temple of Amman)
places.note: Built AD 161 to 166; six 13.5 m portico columns stand, two re-erected. Find the Hand of Hercules, three fingers and an elbow from a statue put at 13 m, then the downtown view from the podium. On the Citadel ticket, so check the price there; 08:00 to 17:00.

places.name: Umayyad Palace
places.note: Governor's residence built about 735 for Caliph Hisham: the cruciform domed hall and monumental gateway (the wooden dome dates from 1998), a bathhouse, a big cistern, and a 6th-century Byzantine church beside it. On the Citadel ticket, so check the price there.

places.name: Jordan Archaeological Museum
places.note: Opened 1951 on the Citadel, prehistoric to 15th-century finds; the plastered skulls from Jericho are the thing to see. The Ain Ghazal statues moved to The Jordan Museum. 45 to 60 minutes, 08:00 to 17:15, about $4.36, free with the Jordan Pass; closing day not confirmed.

places.name: Roman Nymphaeum
places.note: Public fountain of AD 191 dedicated to the Nymphs, recently restored, a few minutes' walk from the Roman Theater. No hours or official price are published; one visitor says it was free once the door was unlocked, so check on the day. 25 minutes.

places.name: Odeon
places.note: 2nd-century Roman odeon of about 500 seats beside the Roman Theater, still used for concerts such as the Al Balad Music Festival. Listed 08:00 to 21:00; no price is published and it may share the Theater ticket, so check the price. 20 minutes.

places.name: Jordanian Museum of Popular Traditions
places.note: Five rooms of East Bank costume, Bedouin jewellery and healing stones, plus Madaba and Jerash mosaics, in the Theater's east wing. On the Theater ticket, so check the price there; free with the Jordan Pass. Fridays 15:00 to 19:00; closed Tuesdays per one listing.

places.name: The Monastery (Ad Deir)
places.note: Carved mid-1st century AD, a 47 m by 48 m facade with an 8 m door. About 800 steps, nearly an hour up past the Lion Triclinium; go late afternoon when the facade is lit, walk rather than ride, and be down by the 17:00 close. On the Petra ticket counted on the Siq row, so check the price there.

places.name: High Place of Sacrifice
places.note: One of Petra's largest cult areas, maybe used since the Edomite Iron Age: carved benches, an altar with baetyls, a blood drain. The stepped trail starts by the Theater; the top looks down on the city and Aaron's tomb. Go mornings. On the Petra ticket counted on the Siq row, so check the price there.
places.neighborhood: Petra Archaeological Park, above the Theater

places.name: Qasr al-Bint (Temple of Dushara)
places.note: Nabataean temple of about 30 BCE, once 23 m tall, one of the few free-standing buildings in Petra. The interior may be closed for archaeological work, so you may only see it from outside; its reliefs are at the Visitor Centre. On the Petra ticket counted on the Siq row, so check the price there.
places.neighborhood: Petra Archaeological Park, end of the Colonnaded Street

places.name: Great Temple
places.note: Big temple complex in the city centre, 4.7 on Google from 489 reviews; the history behind it is thin in what was checked, so treat it as a 40 minute stop on the way to Qasr al-Bint. On the Petra ticket counted on the Siq row, so check the price there.

places.name: Petra Visitor Centre
places.note: Ticket office and guide desk at the gate, free to enter, with reliefs from Qasr al-Bint on show. Opens 06:30, closes 16:00 Saturday and Sunday and 17:00 other days, so hours vary, check. The Petra Museum is 350 m away.
places.neighborhood: Wadi Musa, at the Petra gate

places.name: Seven Pillars of Wisdom
places.note: Seven fluted rock turrets named for T.E. Lawrence's book on the 1916 to 1918 Arab Revolt, seen from the road by the Visitor Centre; best in late afternoon light. Inside the 5 JOD park fee counted on the Visitor Centre row. Komoot lists a 17 km loop.

places.name: Lawrence's House
places.note: A small ruin on Nabataean cistern remains where Lawrence reputedly sheltered; climb the cliff behind for stone towers and wide views. Needs a 4WD, so ask for it on the jeep route. Open access, inside the 5 JOD park fee counted on the Visitor Centre row.

places.name: St George's Church and the Madaba Mosaic Map
places.note: 19th-century church over a 6th-century one whose floor holds the Madaba Map, found 1884, an early map of the Holy Land of about 94 sq m. Climb the tower; parts may be shut for restoration. 3 JOD per a visitor, Jordan Pass cover unconfirmed. Hours vary by day, check.
places.neighborhood: Madaba, about 21 km from the resorts

places.name: Madaba Archaeological Park
places.note: Early Byzantine mosaics including mythological scenes, a stretch of Roman road and Ottoman houses, a few minutes' walk from St George's; about 30 minutes per section. 3 JOD, free with the Jordan Pass per visitors. Listings disagree on hours, so hours vary, check.
places.neighborhood: Madaba, about 21 km from the resorts

places.name: Madaba Museum
places.note: Mosaics of the 5th to 7th centuries, flowers, animals and myth; small, visitors say 15 minutes covers it. 3 JOD per a visitor, free with the Jordan Pass. Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00, closed Saturday and Sunday per one listing, so check.
places.neighborhood: Madaba, about 21 km from the resorts

outings.why: The 45-minute walk through the Siq to the Treasury is the first impression of Petra and it earns the hype, go at opening before the crowds arrive.
outings.name: Petra Treasury & the Siq
outings.fallback: Same walk works any time of day, just crowded midday.

outings.why: Candlelit walk through the Siq to the Treasury with mint tea, slower and less dramatic than the photos suggest but you'd regret skipping it.
outings.name: Petra by Night

outings.why: 800 rock-cut steps to the Monastery plus the Royal Tombs, harder than the Treasury walk and worse on the knees coming down than going up.
outings.name: Ad-Deir Monastery hike

outings.why: Afternoon jeep tour through Lawrence's Spring and Khazali Canyon, some of it staged for photos but the landscape itself is not.
outings.name: Wadi Rum jeep tour

outings.why: Floating is genuinely as strange and fun as advertised, just don't shave or shower with any cut beforehand, it stings badly.
outings.name: Dead Sea float

outings.why: A wade/scramble up a canyon river, the best active thing near the Dead Sea, but it closes without warning after rain and only runs April to October.
outings.name: Wadi Mujib Siq Trail
outings.fallback: Spa-and-float day at the resort, no shame in it.

destination.name: Jordan
destination.pitch: Petra and Wadi Rum back to back is the best desert-and-ruins density in the region, with the Dead Sea as a low-effort finish near the airport.
destination.caveat: Dead Sea resorts genuinely overcharge, and Wadi Mujib only runs April to October so half the year that stretch is spa-and-float only. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.nature: The Wadi Rum desert and the Wadi Mujib canyon trail are two very different landscapes a day apart.
because.culture: Petra is a four-night anchor for a reason, the Siq and Treasury are as good as advertised.
because.adventure: Wadi Rum jeep tours and the Ad-Deir climb are real physical days, not photo-ops dressed up as adventure.
because.relaxation: The Dead Sea float is a genuine do-nothing close to the trip, even if you pay for it.
because.exploration: Ad-Deir's 800 rock-cut steps and Khazali Canyon reward the ones willing to walk further in.
